A1.justification: Both complete 13-page PDFs describe the same research work. Their text, equations, figures and appendices support comparison, including the relocated proofs and v2's additional experimental appendix.

before.justification: Section 5 and Figures 1–2 report original ImageNet classification and SQuAD retrieval experiments comparing the proposed algorithm with four baselines.

after.justification: Section 4 and Appendix B report original classification, retrieval and auction simulation results, including comparisons with DLR.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 retains the same censored-score substitution, empirical CDF, DKW correction and monotone threshold update. SCS is renamed SPS. Changes to the supplied experimental scorers do not change the general proposed algorithm.

E1.justification: ImageNet classification and SQuAD retrieval remain. V2 adds a substantially different task: choosing second-price auction reservation prices subject to a sale-probability requirement, evaluated through simulations using empirical auction bid distributions.

E2.justification: V2 adds the Decaying Learning Rate (DLR) algorithm of Angelopoulos et al. as an evaluated comparator in Figures 1–3. Greedy and ACI remain; ETC and conservative ETC are retained in Appendix B rather than removed.

E3.justification: The reported horizon changes from 3,000 to 10,000 steps. ImageNet scoring changes from ViT probabilities to logits, and DPR scoring changes from softmax-normalized dot products to cosine similarity. Empirical coverage replaces excess prediction set size among the evaluation metrics. These changes prevent interpreting the replacement curves as same-setting performance improvements.

E4.justification: V2 explicitly uses ImageNet logits to investigate sensitivity to scoring-function choice and evaluates DLR under that setting. This adds a limited sensitivity test, but neither paired probability-versus-logit DLR results nor a controlled learning-rate sweep is provided.

E5.justification: V1 specifies averages over 10 runs and 95% bootstrap confidence intervals from 200 resamples. V2 reports averages over 5 runs and removes the confidence-level and bootstrap-method documentation throughout. Any plot shading lacks the previous statistical specification; the PDFs do not establish that uncertainty calculations themselves were discontinued.

E6.justification: V2 replaces the original experimental curves and adds auction, DLR and empirical-coverage outcomes. It reports DLR meeting coverage with zero undercoverage count but higher regret than SPS. V1's excess-set-size results, including the reported 44% and 45% reductions relative to Con-ETC, disappear. The revised scoring functions and horizon make these new results, rather than directly comparable gains.

T1.justification: The main assumptions, regret bound and proofs remain after renumbering Theorem 4.4 to 3.1 and moving the lemmas into Appendix A. V2 adds formal auction payoff/reserve definitions and a randomized full-set/empty-set counterexample. The latter's stated probabilities produce coverage 1−α, although the text describes it as achieving α.

C1.justification: The central semi-bandit, sublinear-regret and coverage claims remain. The abstract, contributions and conclusion extend applicability to auction pricing. Section 1 also explicitly claims the first regret guarantee for threshold convergence and distinguishes the method's PAC-style guarantee from existing marginal guarantees.

C2.justification: V2 substantially expands interpretation of the guarantees through the marginal-versus-PAC distinction and the suitability of i.i.d. assumptions for its intended application. It newly attributes DLR's slow convergence to score scale and learning-rate sensitivity, and its lack of undercoverage to conservative initialization. It also acknowledges that coverage convergence is not separately guaranteed explicitly.

D1.justification: V2 specifies ACI's updates when labels are observed, DLR's learning-rate schedule and the auction simulation's empirical bid sampling. V1's Apple M1 hardware disclosure and 720,000-image fine-tuning detail disappear. V2's less specific description of a pretrained ViT does not establish whether the underlying training actually changed.

R1.justification: The short related-work discussion becomes a substantial comparison covering SAOCP, Conformal PID, decaying-step-size methods, PAC coverage and auction research. V2 recognizes an existing method compatible with limited feedback and shifts the novelty argument toward finite-time regret and stronger coverage guarantees, rather than simply contrasting with methods requiring full labels.

P1.justification: V2 extensively rewrites and expands related work, integrates the main theorem into the algorithm section, relocates preliminary lemmas to Appendix A, and reorganizes five experimental subsections into setup and results. ETC discussion moves to Appendix B, and SCS becomes SPS throughout the narrative.

P2.justification: V1's two figures are replaced by six figures organized into three-task rows and separate main-text and appendix comparator groups. Set-size panels disappear, coverage panels are added, and undercoverage panels are separated. Legends, axes, panel arrangements and captions are substantially revised, with detailed captions replaced by brief metric labels.

improvement.justification: V2 strengthens the evaluation through a relevant semi-bandit-compatible DLR comparator, direct coverage measurements and auction simulations, while improving research positioning. However, it removes direct set-size evidence supporting the central efficiency claim, weakens uncertainty documentation and adds an erroneous coverage counterexample. These material gains and losses leave the net direction of overall quality uncertain.
